claims.statement: Strawson assumes physicalism for argument, treats experience as concrete, and uses physicalism more broadly than exhaustive specification in physics vocabulary.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: His charge that opponents deny experience is not adopted as a verdict on all physicalists.

claims.statement: Strawson argues that structural physical knowledge does not exhaust intrinsic nature, leaving an experiential constitution of brain activity open.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: Compatibility does not establish actuality. Russell/Eddington originals quoted there were not separately inspected.

claims.statement: Strawson requires emergence to depend on the nature of its base, distinguishes metaphysical sufficiency from intelligibility to us, and rejects wholly nonexperiential-to-experiential emergence through a disputed intuition.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: No-radical-emergence is not established by mere experiential/nonexperiential nonidentity. Spatial analogies are not empirical validation.

claims.statement: Experiential ultimates follow conditionally from Strawson’s realism, constitutive-base assumptions and rejection of radical emergence; extending some experiential ultimates to all requires additional homogeneity.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: Micropsychism differs from panpsychism. Certainty of an experience alone does not establish these added premises.

claims.statement: Strawson’s microexperiential constitution framework allows macroqualities unlike constituent qualities, explicitly leaves subject combination and mental causation to explain, and supplies no scientific test in the selected chapter.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: This is an explanatory proposal, not a measured neural realization or law of composition.

claims.statement: The reply’s thin subject cannot exist without current experience, but thinness itself does not entail transience or immortality; identity of subject and experience is a further thesis.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: Strawson’s belief about human transience is not treated as an independently verified empirical result.

claims.statement: Strawson’s developed reply combines object/property and subject/experience identity commitments with experiential ultimates, some pluralities of which constitute numerically distinct larger subjects.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: The metaphysical identities are contested. No criterion specifies which pluralities compose. Not all aggregates are said to experience.

claims.statement: Goff’s direct emergence-parity objection is that microexperiences do not by themselves explain a distinct macrosubject; the avoided brute-emergence burden appears to return.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: A challenge to sufficiency is not by itself a proof of metaphysical impossibility. James is a quoted antecedent, not a separately inspected source.

claims.statement: Goff argues that epistemic limitations about experiential constitution threaten Strawson’s use of transparency to reject ordinary a posteriori physicalist identifications.
source_locators: S-P2T03-002 pp. 54–57, p. 59 n. 2 continuing p. 60
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: His inference from acquaintance in certain respects to stronger transparency is contested. Loar and Strawson 2003 are cited originals not independently inspected here.

claims.statement: Goff’s phenomenal-parthood argument requires experiential constituents to appear as phenomenal parts of the whole and uses slight pains versus a severe pain to challenge novel qualitative summation.
source_locators: S-P2T03-002 pp. 57–59, Phenomenal Parts and Wholes
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: The pain example is stipulated, not a quantitative pain experiment. The experiential-parthood principle is a contested bridge.

claims.statement: Strawson explicitly accepts Goff’s argument as refuting one natural full-revelation smallist interpretation, and answers by distinguishing partial acquaintance from exhaustive disclosure and first-order having from reflective introspection.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: He permits a qualified sense of full disclosure of one’s phenomenal nature; do not report an unqualified rejection of every full-revelation thesis.

claims.statement: The reply allows the constituting experiential event to contain distinct microsubjects whose first-person nature is unavailable to the macrosubject even when its own experiential character is present to it.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: This is a proposed distinction blocking one inference to impossibility, not an explicit constitutive model.

claims.statement: Strawson treats experiences as active substances with causal and constitutive roles; he acknowledges that his schematic argument on pp. 258–259 goes wrong at premise 7.
source_locators: S-P2T03-003 pp. 257–259, especially p. 259 after premise 12
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: The admitted defective argument must not be presented as a sound proof against full revelation.

claims.statement: Strawson proposes that causal powers belong to experiential nature and explicitly relinquishes his earlier characterization of experiential character considered independently of everything else.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: Revision is certified by this reply; no independently verified full comparison with the 2003 original. This is a philosophical cost of the response.

claims.statement: Strawson concedes that he lacks an account of how microexperience constitutes macroexperience; his argument that it occurs is transcendental and assumes smallism, and he acknowledges a formal parity in appeals to prior commitments.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: Unknown laws named by the framework are not supplied laws or established existence proofs.

claims.statement: The selected exchange neither establishes subject combination nor demonstrates its impossibility independently of disputed revelation/parthood premises; an epistemic defense does not discharge the positive constitution burden.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
claims.inference_strength: Bounded conditional assessment, no family ranking
limitations: Limited to these exact versions and selected reply passages. Broader later combination literature uninspected.

claims.statement: Micropsychism and experiential constitution do not entail one cosmic subject, surviving persons, or brain-independent human consciousness; Strawson accepts relevant experiential states as brain states within his account.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: Possibility of a universal subject is left open, not established or ruled out. No survival or process-exclusion experiment is provided.

claims.statement: The supplied chapter treats experience as requiring time, while the reply distinguishes activity from intentional agency; neither statement supplies timelessness, cosmic purpose, goodness or authority.
claims.record_reliability: Direct source attribution within stated edition/locator; unreviewed
limitations: Authorial premises rather than proof about fundamental physics; moral and preservation components not investigated by these texts.

arguments.name: Conditional experiential-ultimate argument
premises: For argument, concrete reality is physical and constituted by physical ultimates.
No experiential reality can emerge from wholly nonexperiential reality.
bridge_principles: Some ultimate constituents must therefore involve experience.
Homogeneity is an additional premise for all ultimates.
arguments.conclusion: Micropsychism, and panpsychism only with added homogeneity, conditional on the premises.
arguments.strongest_objection: Goff: the supposedly explanatory experiential base still needs unexplained subject and quality combination; no-radical-emergence may be an asymmetrically applied intuition.
arguments.strongest_reply: Strawson: same-kind experiential composition may be incomprehensible to us without the metaphysical impossibility he attributes to the wholly nonexperiential case.
unresolved_issues: No independent validation of no-radical-emergence or homogeneity.
No constitution law or actual H-F test.

arguments.name: Goff’s combination and revelation challenge
premises: Many microsubjects do not transparently supply a further subject.
Strawson uses transparent experiential knowledge against ordinary a posteriori identifications.
If experiential being is exhaustively how it feels, a constituent’s experiential character must be part of the whole’s character.
bridge_principles: The needed transparency should apply to both nonexperiential-to-experiential and micro-to-macro transitions.
Wholly additive experiential parts cannot supply qualitatively novel wholes.
arguments.conclusion: The proposed panpsychism has not escaped brute emergence; under the stronger transparency/parthood assumptions novel experiential combination is incoherent.
arguments.strongest_objection: The transparency premise may exceed first-order acquaintance in certain respects; experiential constitution need not be additive or perspective-sharing.
arguments.strongest_reply: Goff: without sufficient transparency, Strawson must explain why ignorance does not equally protect physicalist reduction; footnote 2 extends the concern to experiential nature generally.
unresolved_issues: Goff’s strongest impossibility conclusion is conditional on contested bridges.

arguments.name: Partial acquaintance and active experiential constitution
premises: One has first-order acquaintance with one’s experience without knowing every causal or constitutive feature.
Constituting microsubjects are numerically distinct and need not share their perspectives with the macrosubject.
Experiences are active realities, not passive contents isolated from causal powers.
bridge_principles: Absence of a constituent’s phenomenal character in acquaintance need not establish absence of an experiential constituent.
arguments.conclusion: One full-revelation argument for impossibility can be resisted while experiential composition remains a conditional possibility requiring further account.
arguments.strongest_objection: The revised ontology and ignorance allowance do not explain composition and may weaken the original exclusion of nonexperiential emergence.
arguments.strongest_reply: Strawson acknowledges the concession, rejects exhaustive revelation in the relevant sense, and relies on a transcendental argument with smallism.
unresolved_issues: His pp. 258–259 argument is acknowledged defective.
No positive law specifying subjects, qualities, organization or causal realization.

arguments.name: Equal explanatory standards and component limits
premises: Source-verified attributions do not verify premises.
A conditional experiential ontology can fit neural dependence without a disembodied enduring subject.
Accepted P2T01 and P2T02 supply developed alternatives with distinct unresolved costs.
bridge_principles: Do not confuse constitutive dependence, diachronic causal generation, intrinsic-property identity and distinct-subject ontology.
Require actuality and separate bridges for each component.
arguments.conclusion: Retain experiential constitution as a specified conditional alternative; withhold six-family ranking and all conclusion gates.
arguments.strongest_objection: A defender might regard no-radical-emergence and acquaintance as sufficiently decisive for actual panpsychism.
arguments.strongest_reply: The selected reply explicitly acknowledges intuitive premises, unknown composition and optional universal-subject extension.
unresolved_issues: Broader literature and empirical discriminators not completed.
